subject: TribeLaunch POC: integration recap & schema decisions
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Amir Khan <amir@tribelaunch.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@tribelaunch.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Apr 2028 17:15:00 +0000
Subject: TribeLaunch POC: integration recap & schema decisions

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great conversation. Quick recap and the actions we agreed on for the POC so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: Route live support transcripts through a lightweight policy layer, run embeddings for semantic search, and add a reranker to surface top answers in the support UI.
- Scope for initial sprint: SDK bootstrap (client-side JS + server-side node), auth pattern (service token vs delegated user tokens), routing (region + fallback model policy), and one structured tool-call for external knowledge lookups.

Open questions we flagged on the call (need your confirmation so engineering can scope):
1) Chat vs completions for support summaries: you mentioned short multi-turn summaries — are these always conversational (maintain chat context) or single-shot post-processing of a transcript?
2) Embeddings granularity: do you want sentence-level embeddings on every utterance (higher cost) or paragraph-level (lower cardinality) for reranker input?
3) Tokenization / max_tokens limits: what's the longest transcript you expect per request (est. tokens)? This affects streaming vs batch decisions.
4) Stop sequences & streaming semantics: do you need partial streaming to the UI as tokens arrive, or is batch response acceptable?

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik to send a recommended SDK snippet + auth pattern by Thu 04/05.
- TribeLaunch to share 2 example transcripts (anonymized) by Fri 04/06.
- We’ll provide a draft POC SOW and SSO/token pattern for your security review.

I attached our quickstart and a draft SOW for the sprint. If that matches, I’ll lock the kickoff for Monday.

Best,
Ben

Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Amir Khan <amir@tribelaunch.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@tribelaunch.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Apr 2028 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: TribeLaunch POC: integration recap & schema decisions

Thanks Ben — this is perfect, and yes the summary aligns with our ask. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- Chat vs completions: the front-end will present an aggregated support summary after the agent closes the ticket. It's effectively post-processing of the whole transcript (single-shot), but we may want to iterate to a streaming UX later. For the POC treat it as single-shot completion over the full transcript.
- Embeddings: let's start with sentence-level embeddings for the reranker; accuracy matters more than cost for the POC. We'll optimize later.
- Transcript size: typical transcripts are 400-1,200 words. We estimate ~2.5k tokens max for the longest.
- Streaming: not required for POC; batch is fine.

We'll upload two anonymized transcripts to the Drive link by EOD Thursday. Also sharing our security contact if you need any answers: priyasec@tribelaunch.com.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Amir
Amir Khan
Head of Product, TribeLaunch

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Amir Khan <amir@tribelaunch.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Apr 2028 14:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: TribeLaunch POC: integration recap & schema decisions

Thanks Amir — that helps a lot. Couple of technical recommendations for the single-shot POC based on the transcript size and sentence-level embeddings goal: 

1) SDK + Auth pattern (minimal friction, secure):
- Use server-side Redwood client for ingestion and embedding generation. Client app uploads transcripts to your backend, backend calls Redwood with a service-bound token (rotated via Vault/KMS).
- If you need per-user access later, we can add delegated tokens and short-lived credentials.

2) Chat vs completion & schema:
- For single-shot post-processing, call the completions endpoint with a structured prompt that includes transcript and a JSON schema for output (summary, TL;DR, tags).
- Example: request with "max_tokens" tuned to ~250 for a ~2.5k token input; use the runtime's structured output annotations so you get a machine-parseable JSON back rather than free text.

3) Tokenization & truncation:
- We recommend pre-tokenizing on your side to measure token counts and chunking long transcripts into overlapping windows if > 3k tokens.
- For embeddings: create sentence-level chunks, but drop very short (<5 word) spans to reduce noise.

4) Reranker flow:
- Build embeddings for sentence chunks, store in your vector DB (we support direct outputs to common stores).
- For reranker input, assemble top-K candidates by cosine score, then call a reranker model (completion with candidate list) using a short context — this improves precision.

5) Streaming: since POC is batch, we'll disable streaming. The SDK supports streaming later with incremental tooling (useful for live agent UX).

I attached a short SDK snippet and sample prompt template.

—Karthik

Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 06 Apr 2028 11:07:00 -0700

Appreciate the detailed notes. Two small follow-ups from security/engineering: 

- Max_tokens safety: if we submit a single 2.5k token transcript + instructions, are there any hard model limits we should be aware of? Do you automatically reject or truncate when > model context?
- Stop sequences: for structured JSON outputs, will the completion endpoint guarantee valid JSON if we provide a schema and stop tokens? We’ve seen partial streaming results break parsers in other systems.

If you can confirm behavior we’ll finalize the SOW.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Engineering Lead, TribeLaunch
priyasec@tribelaunch.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priyasec@tribelaunch.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Apr 2028 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: TribeLaunch POC: integration recap & schema decisions

Great questions Priya — answers below: 

- Model context & hard limits: each model has a documented context window. If a request exceeds that, our API returns a clear error ("context_length_exceeded") rather than silently truncating. We also provide a preflight token-count endpoint so you can estimate token usage before calling completion. For your numbers (<=2.5k tokens) the recommended midsize models comfortably support a 4k+ context window; we'll recommend one in the SOW.

- Structured JSON + stop behavior: when you use the structured output feature with an attached schema, the runtime validates the model output against the schema and will retry generation up to N times if it detects malformed JSON (with configurable retry behavior). For streaming responses, the SDK can buffer until a complete schema-valid payload is available; streaming partial tokens to the UI without buffering is possible but we don't recommend it for machine-parseable JSON.

Operational tips:
- Set a conservative "max_tokens" for the response section (e.g., 300) and use completion penalties to keep summaries concise.
- Use explicit stop sequences for freeform outputs, but rely on schema validation for machine responses.

If that works I’ll update the SOW to call out model selection (4k context), token preflight steps, and the schema-validation retry policy.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
